Former NIU head football coach Joe Novak dies at 81

Joe Novak speaks at a podium during his retirement press conference in November 2007 at the Yordon Center. Novak led NIU to five consecutive winning seasons, earned Mid-American Conference Coach of the Year honors in 2002 and was inducted into the NIU Athletics Hall of Fame in 2013. (Courtesy of NIU Athletics)
By Kristopher Houston, Sports Editor
Jul 29, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:25
Instaread

From winning MAC Coach of the Year in 2002, to getting inducted into the NIU Athletics Hall of Fame in 2013, former head coach Joe Novak left a mark on Huskie football that won’t be forgotten.

As he came into a program that had been underperforming, going 3-8 in 1995 prior to the beginning of the Novak era, Novak knew he had work to do. 

After a rough 8-36 four-year start to his career, Novak’s back was against the wall. Looking to find a lifeline and successfully turn NIU football around, he struck gold at the turn of the century. 

In the 2000-2001 season, the Novak-led Huskies went 6-5, beating many expectations.

NIU football then followed this success with five consecutive seasons with winning records, going 47-25 with two bowl games in the span of six years.

In 2003 came some of the most notable wins in program history, stunning Power 6 schools University of Alabama and University of Maryland at the time with NIU going 10-2 on the season.

After arguably the most successful run in NIU football coaching history, Novak spent his last year as a head coach in 2007 at the age of 62.

While most were not ready for the Novak era to end, many never questioned that the Ohio native gave Northern Illinois everything he had. 

Novak died on Tuesday. His cause of death has yet to be released.
